topics.title: QUAD FM Meeting
bullets: The foreign ministers of the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) met at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on 26 May 2026 to launch a series of major initiatives.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar chaired the session, which focused on maritime surveillance, port infrastructure, critical minerals, and regional energy security.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the meeting’s outcomes as “real concrete achievables”, highlighting the Quad’s transformation into a “partnership of action”. What is the QUAD? –

The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad) started as an informal partnership after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, when India, Australia, Japan and the US coordinated humanitarian and disaster relief.
It was officially proposed by former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2007, but became inactive for almost a decade due to Australian concerns about provoking China.
The Quad was revived in 2017 reflecting evolving regional views on China’s expanding influence, and has since held multiple foreign ministers’ meetings and leaders’ summits.
September 2021: The then US President Biden hosted the first in- person Quad Leaders’ Summit in Washington with PM Modi, PM Morrison and PM Suga.
May 2023: The then Australian PM Albanese hosted the Quad Leaders’ Summit in Hiroshima with PM Modi, PM Kishida and President Biden.
Since 2019, the Quad foreign ministers have gathered eight times, with five top-level summits held since March 2021. QUAD FM Meeting
The Quad aims to counterbalance China’s growing geopolitical and economic influence in the Indo-Pacific region by presenting a united front of democratic nations.
It seeks to ensure security and freedom of navigation in critical maritime routes, such as the South China Sea, which are essential for international trade.
The group focuses on fostering economic development, infrastructure projects, technology innovation, and addressing global challenges like pandemics and climate change.
Approximately one-third of the world’s shipping passes through the South China Sea, which is rich in fish and fossil fuels, making it a strategic zone contested by regional powers.
China claims over 80% of the South China Sea based on the “nine-dash line” , overlapping with internationally recognised territories of Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and the Philippines.
The Quad has consistently opposed “intimidating manoeuvres” and the militarisation of disputed features, reaffirming adherence to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982. Quad Plus –

It refers to the expansion of the Quad dialogue to include other like-minded countries on specific issues, such as South Korea, Vietnam, and New Zealand, who joined weekly Quad meetings in March 2020.
In May 2020, the US hosted a meeting with Quad nations along with Brazil, Israel and South Korea to discuss a global response to COVID-19.
Quad Plus focuses on global issues like pandemics, whereas the Quad deals primarily with security concerns in maritime, technology and infrastructure.
Quad Plus provides a multipolar perspective for examining and evaluating the strategic multilateral expansion of the participating nations.
It could lay the groundwork for future expansion or collaborations in the region.
Quad Plus links the four founding nations with emerging global powers through initiatives that support regional prosperity, peace, and stability. IMPDA –
The Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness was launched at the 2022 Quad Leaders’ Summit in Tokyo to enhance maritime domain awareness capabilities in the Indo-Pacific region.
It is a technology and training initiative that provides near-real-time commercial satellite tracking data to countries across Southeast Asia, the Indian Ocean region, and the Pacific.
The Quad has initiated regional pilots to deliver radio frequency data to maritime agencies, helping combat illegal fishing, trafficking and supporting humanitarian disaster response.
On September 21, 2024, US President Biden hosted PM Modi, PM Albanese, and PM Kishida in Wilmington, Delaware, after India swapped hosting rights.
The summit launched the Quad Cancer Moonshot, MAITRI, Quad Ports of the Future Partnership, a 2025 Quad-at-Sea Mission, and a semiconductor supply chain network.
Leaders committed to securing Quad funding, creating a US Congressional Quad Caucus, and holding the first Quad Commerce and Industry Ministers meeting. India – Japan Bilateral Exercises
Malabar Exercise: Naval drills involving India, Japan, the US (and Australia) for maritime security and interoperability.
Dharma Guardian: Annual counter-terrorism exercise between the Indian and Japanese armies.
Shinyuu Maitri: Air force exercise focusing on air defence, disaster response and humanitarian assistance. India – Australia Bilateral Exercises
AUSINDEX: Joint naval exercise focusing on maritime operations, anti-submarine warfare and security.
PITCH BLACK: Air force exercise enhancing tactical air operations and interoperability among participating nations.
TAHWEI: Army exercise involving training in counter-terrorism and peacekeeping operations. India – US Bilateral Exercises
Yudh Abhyas: Army counter-terrorism training exercise held annually.
Vajra Prahar: Special forces counter-terrorism exercise focused on joint planning and operations.
Cope India: Air combat training exercise between the Indian and US Air Forces.
Tiger Triumph: Joint tri-service disaster relief exercise. Recent Meeting –
It was attended by EAM S. Jaishankar (India), US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong, and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi.
This was the third Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting in a short span (January 2025, July 2025, and now May 2026), demonstrating the group’s sustained engagement.
The ministers devoted a large part of their exchanges to analysing the “current state of the world” , with a specific focus on the Indo-Pacific.
The Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Corporation initiative was launched to leverage each country’s surveillance assets to enhance information sharing.
The IPMDA was expanded to the Indian Ocean, providing near-real-time unclassified satellite tracking data to combat illegal fishing, trafficking, and support disaster response.
India committed to hosting the next Quad at Sea Mission, bringing together coast guards of all four nations on a single ship.
The Quad announced its first-ever joint port infrastructure project under the Quad Ports of the Future Partnership, with a pilot project to advance port infrastructure in Fiji.
This directly addresses insufficient port capacity in the Pacific Islands and is a practical demonstration of the Quad’s ability to deliver high-quality, resilient infrastructure.
It is expected to serve as a model for other projects in the region in the future.
The ministers launched the Quad Critical Minerals Initiative framework to strengthen supply chains for critical minerals, including mining, processing and recycling.
The initiative aims to coordinate investment and leverage economic policy tools to reduce dependence on single sources (implicitly China).
It reflects growing concern over the export restrictions of critical minerals by certain countries, which can destabilise global supply chains.
The Quad initiative on Indo-Pacific energy security was announced to strengthen regional energy resilience, especially in light of the Iranian closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
The partners will identify areas of cooperation in technology, management, policy, market analysis and emergency response exercises.
The US Department of Energy will host a fuel security forum later in 2026 to further expand on this initiative.
The joint statement after the meeting did not identify the host country for the next leaders’ Summit (which was due to be held in India), sparking speculation about the group’s future.

Officials cited difficulty in pinning down leaders’ schedules, with the Summit possibly being held on the sidelines of other multilateral meetings like the UN General Assembly or G-20 Summit in the US in December.
Australia will now host the next Foreign Ministers’ meeting, as India will hand over the chair of the grouping.
China has consistently opposed the Quad, describing it as an attempt to create “exclusive small cliques” that undermine regional cooperation.
Beijing views the Quad as a US-led containment strategy aimed at countering its rise, and has warned against the militarisation of the South China Sea.

Despite Quad statements, China continues to assert its claims in the South China Sea and has increased its maritime militia activities in the region. PASSAGE: The controversy surrounding the Delhi Gymkhana Club in 2026 has reignited debate over land governance, elite institutions, and public property regulation in India. The Union government sought repossession of the club premises situated in Lutyens’ Delhi, citing lease, administrative, and public land considerations. The move triggered legal proceedings and wider discussion regarding the use of government land by private institutions. The Delhi Gymkhana Club, established during the colonial period, occupies a prominent site in New Delhi and has historically been associated with senior bureaucrats, military officers, diplomats, and business elites. The dispute has raised broader questions concerning leasehold rights, transparency, accountability, and regulation of organisations occupying public land. Source: Indian Express
